academic_translation:
For an entity that exists,
What need is there for a cause?
Yet even if it does not exist,
What need is there for a cause?
translation: If a thing already exists, why does it need a cause? But even if it does not exist, why does it need a cause?

academic_translation:
Even by hundreds of millions of causes,
A non-entity cannot be transformed.
How could that state be an entity?
And what else could become an entity?
translation: Even millions of causes cannot change a non-existent thing. How could a non-existent thing ever become real? And what else could become a thing?

academic_translation:
If an entity cannot exist at the time of non-existence,
When will it become an existent entity?
Without an entity having been produced,
It will not separate from that non-entity.
translation: If a thing cannot exist when it does not exist, when will it ever become a thing? Until a thing is made, it cannot separate from being a non-existent thing.

academic_translation:
If it does not separate from non-entity,
There is no opportunity for an entity to exist.
An entity also does not become non-existent,
Because it would follow that it has two natures.
translation: If it does not separate from being a non-existent thing, there is no chance for a thing to exist. A thing also cannot become non-existent. If it did, it would have two natures.

academic_translation:
Thus, there is no cessation,
And there is also no entity; therefore,
All these wandering beings
Are always unborn and unceasing.
translation: So, there is no stopping, and there is no thing. Therefore, all these beings are always never born and never ending.

academic_translation:
Wandering beings are like a dream;
When analyzed, they are like a plantain tree.
Even between nirvāṇa and not passing into nirvāṇa,
In reality, there is no distinction.
translation: Beings are like a dream. When we look closely, they are like a banana tree. In the way things really are, there is no difference between finding freedom from sorrow and not finding it.

academic_translation:
Thus, regarding entities that are empty,
What is there to gain and what is there to lose?
In being honored by anyone,
Or being utterly despised, what is there?
translation: Since things are empty, what is there to gain and what is there to lose? What does it matter if someone honors you or treats you badly?

academic_translation:
From what do happiness and suffering arise?
What is there to be displeased about, what is there to be pleased about?
When searched for in reality,
Who is craving, and for what are they craving?
translation: Where do happiness and suffering come from? What is there to be upset or happy about? If I look for the way things really are, who is wanting? And what are they wanting?

academic_translation:
When analyzed, in this world of the living,
Who is it that will die here?
What will come to be, and what has been?
And who is a relative, and who is a friend?
translation: If I look closely at this world of living beings, who will die here? What will happen, and what has happened? Who is a relative, and who is a friend?

academic_translation:
May those like me completely grasp
That everything is like space.
Those who desire happiness for themselves,
Through causes of conflict and excitement,
translation: I hope people like me completely understand that everything is like space. People who want happiness for themselves find causes for fighting and excitement.

academic_translation:
Become greatly agitated and delighted.
With grief, exertion, and dispute,
Mutually cutting and piercing one another,
And through misdeeds, they live in great hardship.
translation: They get very upset and very happy. With sadness, hard work, and arguing, they cut and pierce each other. Through harmful deeds, they live a very hard life.

academic_translation:
Having come again and again to happy realms,
And having enjoyed much happiness,
After dying, they fall into the sufferings
Of the lower realms, which are long-lasting and unbearable.
translation: They come to happy realms again and again, enjoying a lot of happiness. But after they die, they fall into the sufferings of the unhappy realms. These sufferings are terrible and last a very long time.

academic_translation:
In existence, there are many precipices,
And there, what is not reality is like this.
Because there is also mutual contradiction there,
In existence, there is no such reality.
translation: In life, there are many steep cliffs. There, what is not the way things really are is like this. Because things clash with each other there, in life there is no such thing as the way things really are.

academic_translation:
There too, the incomparable, unbearable
Ocean of suffering is boundless.
There, one thus has little strength,
And there, the lifespan is also short.
translation: In that place, the ocean of suffering is huge and too hard to bear. It has no edge. There, people have very little strength, and their lives are short.

academic_translation:
Even there, through activities for survival
And health, the weariness of hunger,
Sleep, harm, and likewise
Meaningless association with childish persons,
translation: Even there, we spend our time just trying to stay alive and healthy. We get tired from hunger, sleep, and being hurt. We also waste time with foolish persons.

academic_translation:
Life passes quickly and meaninglessly,
And analysis is extremely hard to find.
Even there, as for habituation to distraction,
Where is the means to reverse it?
translation: Life passes by fast and has no meaning. Careful thinking is very hard to find. Since we are so used to distraction there, how can we ever stop it?

academic_translation:
Even there, into the great lower realm,
Māra exerts himself to make one fall.
There, wrong paths are many,
And it is hard to overcome even doubt.
translation: Even there, Mara works hard to make us fall into the great unhappy realm. There are many wrong paths, and it is hard to overcome even doubt.

academic_translation:
Once again, leisure is hard to find,
And a Buddha's appearance is extremely hard to find.
The river of afflictions is hard to abandon;
Alas, suffering will continue in succession!
translation: Once again, the freedom to practice is hard to find. It is very hard to find a time when a Buddha appears. The river of troubling emotions is hard to leave behind. Sadly, suffering will just keep going on and on!

academic_translation:
Even though they are thus in extreme suffering,
Those who do not see their own suffering—
These beings dwelling in the river of suffering,
Alas, are worthy of lamentation!
translation: Even though they suffer so much, some beings do not see their own pain. We should feel very sad for those who live in the river of suffering!

academic_translation:
For example, just as some bathe again and again
And then repeatedly enter a fire,
Likewise, although dwelling in extreme suffering,
They pride themselves on being happy.
translation: For example, some people wash themselves again and again, but then walk right back into a fire. In the same way, some people live in terrible pain but still think they are happy.

academic_translation:
Thus, for those who abide acting
As if there were no aging and death,
First of all, they will be killed,
And then the unbearable fall into the lower realms will come.
translation: Some people act as if there is no growing old and dying. First they will be killed. Then they will take a terrible fall into an unhappy realm.

academic_translation:
Thus, for those tormented by the fire of suffering,
Well-arisen from the clouds of merit—
With a rain of my own accumulation of happiness—
When will I pacify them?
translation: When will I use a rain of my own happiness to bring peace to those burning in the fire of suffering? This rain will fall from clouds made of my store of goodness.

academic_translation:
When, in the manner of non-apprehension,
Having respectfully gathered the accumulation of merit,
To those who are ruined by apprehension,
Will I teach emptiness?
translation: When will I respectfully build up my gathered store of goodness while not fixing on anything? And when will I teach emptiness to those who are ruined by fixing on something?

academic_translation: From Entering the Way of the Bodhisattva, the ninth chapter, the Perfection of Wisdom.

locked_terms.use: Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero

translation: From Entering the Way of the Awakening Hero, this is the ninth chapter, called the Perfection of Wisdom.

academic_translation:
In my having composed
Engaging in the Conduct of Awakening,
Through whatever virtue there is, may all wandering beings
Engage in the conduct of awakening.
translation: I have written this book about the way of acting for awakening. By this good deed, may every being begin the way of acting for awakening.

academic_translation:
In all directions, however many there are
Sick with the suffering of body and mind,
May they, through my merit,
Attain an ocean of happiness and joy.
translation: There are beings everywhere sick with suffering in their bodies and minds. By my store of goodness, may they find an ocean of happiness and joy.

academic_translation:
For as long as they remain in saṃsāra,
May they never decline from happiness.
May wandering beings attain a bodhisattva's
Uninterrupted happiness.
translation: As long as they remain in the cycle of rebirth, may they never lose their happiness. May every being reach the unbroken happiness of an awakening hero.

academic_translation:
In the world systems, the hells,
However many there are,
In them, may embodied beings
Rejoice with the happiness of Sukhavati.
translation: There are many hells in the world realms. May every being with a body there rejoice with the happiness of Sukhavati.

academic_translation:
May those tormented by cold attain warmth.
From the great clouds of the bodhisattvas,
Through the boundless rivers that have arisen,
May those tormented by heat be cooled.
translation: May those hurt by cold find warmth. Endless rivers flow from the great clouds of the awakening heroes. May those rivers cool everyone hurt by heat.

academic_translation:
May the forest of sword-leaves also
Become a dense sandalwood forest for them.
May the trunks of the śālmali trees also
Grow into wish-fulfilling trees.
translation: May the forest of sword leaves become a thick sandalwood forest for them. May the trunks of the Shalmali trees also grow into wish-granting trees.

academic_translation:
May they be beautified by the sweet calls
Of waterfowl, ruddy geese, swans, cranes, and so forth,
And may the regions of hell become delightful
With lakes possessing greatly fragrant lotuses.
translation: May sweet songs of water birds like swans and geese make these places beautiful. May the regions of hell become wonderful. May they have lakes filled with sweet-smelling lotus flowers.

academic_translation:
May those heaps of coals become heaps of jewels,
May the scorched earth become a leveled crystal floor,
And may the mountains of the Crushing Hell also become
Celestial palaces of offerings, filled with Sugatas.
translation: May the heaps of hot coals become heaps of jewels. May the burned ground become a smooth floor of crystal. May the mountains of the Crushing Hell become heavenly palaces of offerings. May they be filled with Well-Gone Ones.

academic_translation:
May the rain of embers, burning stones, and weapons
From now on become a rain of flowers,
And may that striking of one another with weapons
From now on become a tossing of flowers in play.
translation: May the rain of hot coals, burning stones, and weapons become a rain of flowers. Instead of striking each other with weapons, may they now toss flowers at each other in play.

academic_translation:
May those submerged in the unfordable river that is like a fire pit,
Their flesh all destroyed and their bones the color of kunda flowers,
By the power of my virtue attain the bodies of gods,
And abide together with goddesses in the gently flowing river.
translation: Some beings are trapped in a fiery river that cannot be crossed. Their flesh is gone and their bones are the color of kunda flowers. By the power of my good deeds, may they get the bodies of gods. May they live with goddesses in a gently flowing river.

academic_translation:
"Why are the men of Yama, and the unbearable crows and vultures terrified here?
Whose noble power is this that dispels darkness everywhere and generates bliss and joy?"
Thinking thus, looking upward, and seeing the blazing Vajrapāṇi residing in the midst of the sky,
Freed from misdeeds by the force of intense joy, may they accompany him.
translation: "Why are the men of Yama and the terrible crows and vultures so afraid? Whose great power chases away the dark and brings joy?" Thinking this, they look up and see blazing Vajrapani in the sky. May great joy free them from their harmful deeds. May they go with him.

academic_translation:
By the falling of a rain of flowers mixed with scented water,
Seeing the fires and embers of hell extinguished with a hiss,
And thinking, "What is this sudden satisfaction with bliss?"
May the hell beings behold Padmapāṇi.
translation: A rain of flowers and sweet-smelling water falls. The fires and hot coals of hell go out with a hiss. Wondering, "Where does this sudden happiness come from?" may the hell beings look up and see Padmapani.

academic_translation:
"Friends, cast away fear and come quickly here to us!
By whose power we are freed from all suffering and the force of joy arrives,
He who thoroughly protects all wandering beings, who has given rise to bodhicitta and affection—
Who is this blazing youth with a topknot who arrives to make us fearless?"
translation: "Friends, throw away your fear and come quickly to us! His power frees us from all suffering and brings us joy. He protects all beings. He has the awakening mind and compassion. Who is this glowing boy with a topknot coming to make us fearless?"

academic_translation:
"You, look at this one whose lotus feet the crowns of a hundred gods worship,
Whose eyes are moistened with compassion, and upon whose head a rain of multitudes of flowers falls,
Endowed with delightful tiered palaces and thousands of goddesses proclaiming songs of praise!"
Upon seeing Mañjuśrī like this, may the hell beings now cry out in joy.
translation: "Look at him! The crowns of a hundred gods bow to his feet. His eyes are wet with compassion, and a rain of flowers falls on his head. He has beautiful palaces and thousands of goddesses singing his praise!" When they see Manjushri like this, may the hell beings shout with joy.

academic_translation:
Likewise, by my roots of virtue, upon seeing Samantabhadra and other
Bodhisattvas' unobstructed clouds, and the blissful,
Cool, fragrant rain they let fall,
May those sentient beings of hell become manifestly joyful.
translation: Through my roots of good deeds, may the living beings of hell see Samantabhadra and other awakening heroes. These heroes bring happy clouds and let a cool, sweet-smelling rain fall. When the living beings see this, may they be filled with joy.

academic_translation:
May animals be freed
From the fear of eating one another,
And just like the humans of Uttarakuru,
May the hungry ghosts become happy.
translation: May animals be free from the fear of eating each other. Just like the people of Uttarakuru, may the hungry ghosts be happy.
